behaviour: The append-only logs are two hash-chained JSONL streams, events and evidence, merged by union in git.
The agent is kept from running plumb approve by declarative deny rules plus the CLI session-marker check.
An approval the agent relays is recorded by plumb relay; plumb approve is the owner's alone.
Prompt digests go to gitignored session state and are copied into the committed log only when an approval cites them.
Each test run appends one compact evidence entry to the committed evidence log; the cache holds only a reuse index.
The stop hook blocks once per turn asking the agent to run the changed covering tests; the hook never runs pytest.
note: Test time allowance later set by DEC-078.

behaviour: The sub-project 1 commands are validate, tests map, tests run, hooks install and statusline, with concept names as aliases.
The session brief is about 30 lines with a hard cap of 40.
Per-turn tests have a 15 s budget with a hard limit of 1.5 times that.
note: DEC-078 sets covering tests at 60 s per turn.

behaviour: A test node that passed or flaked earlier and now fails is a regression even if its source changed; only a new red test is exempt.
The minimal importer brings every imported record in as proposed, never approved.
Links are stored in their source record's links list, with plumb link as the command.
Sub-project 1 is built core first, then bootstrap, then three lanes in parallel.
Sub-projects 2 to 5 are built by a contracts phase alone, then five lanes in parallel on disjoint files.
The importer completion's requirements sit in FEAT-004 beside the other host adapters.
note: Placement decision for a past build.

behaviour: Only the owner turns auto-approval on or off, through a logged config event the agent can never write.
note: Later DEC-064/073 govern what auto-approval covers.

behaviour: One grouped confirmation line names up to five records, then +N more, and the owner's ok approves exactly that pinned list.
note: DEC-067 asks once per principle; related.

behaviour: Calibration per record kind needs 20 owner decisions and 5 'no' examples, with JEV wrongly accepting none and accepting half of confirmed records.
Triage, config and jev commands and their data are built in capture; their owner-facing views in the presentation lane.
An intent conflict is recorded inside the conflicted record as a conflict block with an IC id.
Git's merge completes with the conflicted record unconfirmed, and the merge check holds it until the owner chooses.
On an ID collision the first-parent branch keeps its IDs and the incoming record is renumbered.
The plugin carries a ready-built plumb checked against source and sets up a private per-user, per-version copy of its tools.
Background checks do the recording and guarding; the in-app panel draws the band and cards from what they recorded.
A button press is proven by a random secret held only in the panel's memory, which the agent's shell cannot use.
A rejected read-back is recaptured always; it counts as a calibration no only when the owner says it misread them.
A small model run through the host's dispatch, never the coding agent, reads the owner's messages for approvals and rejections.
note: DEC-058 removes the automatic check; DEC-069 keeps understand.model.

behaviour: Long-running progress shows as a terminal bar or plain lines and also in the Claude Code status line.
The proposed backlog is judged in one background pass and shown as one card per feature.
Settling switches on by itself once calibrated for agent-derived records, but the owner switches it on for intents.
note: DEC-040 removes settling by context; DEC-073 sets verdict confirmation.

behaviour: Work order puts SP7 re-alignment in parallel with the everyday loop in separate worktrees.
Ask for a change puts the cursor in the message box prefilled with the topic, and the typed words are read against that card.
No appears as a button only where the card suggests it, beside Ask for a change and Leave open.
Leave open stops a card repeating at turn end until its record changes, while it stays listed as awaiting the owner.
The Claude Code mod is built in parallel with slice 3 after the press and plugin slices.
The grounding skill is named plumb-records so /plumb means one thing.
A missing proof does not block a merge; plumb names it and the owner decides.
The judge keeps being calibrated with at most three open trial cards in the read-back shape.
A question the agent can recommend on becomes a flippable assumption; only an unrecommendable costly question blocks the build.
One judge reads the owner's words, calibrated by trial cards; settling by context is removed.
Diagrams use the architecture-diagram skill: instructions and a template, with the agent writing the SVG.
note: DEC-047 has the diagram mod supply the renderer.

behaviour: The diagram mod lives in its own repository, used beside plumb.
The clarify check receives the agent's last reply, recent messages and repository facts, resolving references to earlier turns.
note: Merge-conflict choice between two SR-128 versions.
